lesson.title: Opstaan, Wassen & Slapen
lesson.subtitle: a full day told through reflexive and separable verbs

hook.title: A Day in Order
hook.content: Opstaan, aankleden, wassen, eten, werken, slapen: a Dutch day is a chain of verbs, many of them reflexive or separable. The order of the day is also the order of the sentence.

pattern.title: Finite verb second, prefix or infinitive last
pattern.content: Ik sta om zeven uur op, ik kleed me aan, ik was me, ik ga slapen. Separable prefixes and infinitives close their clauses; the reflexive follows the finite verb.
pattern.trap_note: With opstaan, the prefix op goes to the end: ik sta op, not ik opsta in a main clause.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Opstaan, Wassen & Slapen):
exercises.target_answer: opstaan, aankleden, wassen, eten, werken, slapen
exercises.meaning: to get up, to dress, to wash, to eat, to work, to sleep
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Opstaan, Wassen & Slapen": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I get up at seven.”?
options: Ik sta om zeven uur op.
niet Ik sta om zeven uur op.
Ik sta om zeven uur op. (1)
exercises.target_answer: Ik sta om zeven uur op.
exercises.explanation: “Ik sta om zeven uur op.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Opstaan, Wassen & Slapen”.

cues: The pattern: Finite verb second, prefix or infinitive last
exercises.explanation: “Ik kleed me aan.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Finite verb second, prefix or infinitive last.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: With opstaan, the prefix op goes to the end: ik sta op, not ik opsta in a main clause.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik was me.” is word-for-word “I wash me.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Finite verb second, prefix or infinitive last.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: I am going to sleep.
exercises.explanation: “Ik ga slapen.” reuses only material taught in “Opstaan, Wassen & Slapen” — Finite verb second, prefix or infinitive last.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Ik ga slapen.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Finite verb second, prefix or infinitive last.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I eat bread.”
twist.explanation: A plain main clause in the middle of the routine; the frame is still V2.

summary.outcome: Narrate a daily routine with separable and reflexive verbs.
summary.takeaway: A routine is a sequence of brackets: finite verb early, prefix or infinitive late.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Omdat, Maar & Hoewel.

opstaan.context_phrase: Ik sta om zeven uur op.

aankleden.etymology_derivation: Separable: aan + kleden ('clothe'), with a reflexive pronoun.

wassen.etymology_derivation: English wash and Dutch wassen are the same verb.

eten.etymology_derivation: English eat and Dutch eten are the same verb; German shifted t to ss in essen.

werken.etymology_derivation: English work and Dutch werken are the same verb.

slapen.etymology_derivation: English sleep and Dutch slapen are the same verb; German shifted p to f in schlafen.
